heuristic.applicability: Prefer blue_insert__h04 when the drawer is open, red is on or being released over its pad, and translation of the free blue or a changed source-to-destination separation is the main risk. It remains callable throughout the full assigned overlap and later insertion. h02 remains the safer library choice for nominal or stable carried-blue states where destination anchoring dominates; h01 better covers a rotated source because h04 guarantees translation covariance only; h03 remains complementary for small fresh-TCP tracking deviations.

handoff.entry_conditions: drawer_position is strictly above 0.26 m; red is on or being released over the outside pad; blue is outside, approached, or carried; source_object resolves to observed blue_pose and destination_field resolves to blue_goal. At earliest entry, fingers may still be closed around red, so closure is not evidence of a blue grasp.
handoff.exit_conditions: Use the unchanged simultaneous evaluator condition at one observation: drawer_position strictly above 0.26 m, red fully contained on its pad with center z in (0.014,0.031) m, and blue fully contained in the drawer cavity with center z in (0.053,0.074) m. Release and high retreat are demonstrated context, not additional success requirements.
handoff.failure_signatures: Predicted progress alpha selects the wrong corridor anchor; a source displacement drags red-release targets toward blue; pickup is pulled toward the destination before a grasp; blue does not co-move after closure; reconstructed targets are unreachable or IK reports residual/limits; blue approaches a wall/lip; drawer closes to 0.26 m or below; red leaves the pad; or final blue containment/z fails.
handoff.overlap_role: Preserve every action in every [600,stop) segment, including all 250 actions from 600 through 849 in each trajectory shared with red_transfer: 3,000 supervised overlap actions covering red lowering/release, retreat, transit, blue approach, closure, and lift. The corridor coordinate is trained over this overlap rather than only over final insertion.
handoff.successor_readiness: There is no learned manipulation successor. Continue through insertion and the demonstrated release/retreat when appropriate, then defer to the unchanged framework success evaluator. If a stable carried blue is near the drawer and progress anchoring is uncertain, h02 is the preferred complementary continuation.

heuristic.limitations: Translation covariance of decoded targets does not make shifted scenes reachable or collision-free and does not establish grasp/contact. World-frame orientation is not invariant to blue or drawer rotation. Alpha is predicted and can be wrong under unseen phase/contact states. Cross-track residuals are learned only from nominal paths. The observed blue reference is frozen for an eight-action chunk, so slip is incorporated at the next replan. Demonstrations contain no drops, re-grasps, wall impacts, or recovery.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Use the unchanged DiffusionBackbone with a 106-value condition from two causal 53-D structured feature frames and an 11-D Cartesian action. Each slot is [alpha, residual_position_world_m(3), world_rotation_6d(6), gripper(1)]. Representation normalization is fitted only to valid transformed training labels. decode_action clips alpha to [0,1], reconstructs a world TCP pose, projects 6-D rotation to SO(3), and calls only panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh joints. No augmentation, future inference input, auxiliary head, recurrent state, or backbone change is needed.
heuristic.rationale: Observed validation was 10/12 for the full blue-frame h01, 12/12 for destination-frame h02, and 10/12 for fresh-TCP h03; failures always missed blue_inside while retaining drawer and red conditions. No OOD result exists. The new independent policy tests a different representational hypothesis: for each commanded target p, calculate alpha=clip(dot(p-b,g-b)/||g-b||^2,0,1), anchor=b+alpha(g-b), and residual=p-anchor, using causal chunk-start blue position b and goal g. Pickup targets near alpha=0 move exactly with source translation; insertion targets near alpha=1 remain goal anchored; intermediate carry targets warp continuously. Red-release targets that project toward the goal end avoid the full source translation that h01 applies to every phase. This combines source-displacement coverage with the destination anchoring associated with the strongest nominal validation, without claiming that result proves OOD benefit.
heuristic.statement: Learn world Cartesian TCP targets in a continuous source-to-destination corridor coordinate: diffuse a per-slot progress alpha, cross-track/vertical world residual, world 6-D orientation, and gripper scalar. This targets translated blue pickup by construction while preserving destination-relative insertion and reducing inappropriate source anchoring during predecessor red release.

assignment.subgoal: Primary responsibility: finish the predecessor red release/retreat context, acquire the blue block outside the drawer, lift and transport it to the open drawer cavity, lower it inside, release it, and retreat to a high clear pose. The intended object is blue; the red block visible at segment entry is only the predecessor object still being lowered/released. Observed contact/motion: at observation 600 red is still pinched near the pad at z about 0.032-0.037 m; by 700 red is settled at z about 0.020 m and the open gripper is retreating toward blue; around 800 the TCP descends over blue; by 850 blue is pinched and lifted; later it is carried to the drawer, lowered to z about 0.063 m, released, and the TCP retreats to z about 0.323 m. Final observations in all occurrences simultaneously show drawer_position about 0.297, red near (-0.176 to -0.177,-0.298 to -0.304,0.020), and blue near (-0.171 to -0.173,0.073 to 0.074,0.063), satisfying the supplied one-observation completion rule. The demo1000 final front image supports blue in the drawer, red on the outside pad, and the open drawer. Purpose/expected benefit: retaining the long release-to-pick overlap should make this independently trained insertion model usable from intermediate transition states; demonstrated success does not establish recovery from dropped blue blocks, drawer collisions, or unseen placements.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: For encoded labels, clipped progress plus residual reconstructs the demonstrated commanded world TCP position exactly, including the near-coincident endpoint convention. Compare decoded FK position in metres, rotation angle in radians and gripper scalar to that commanded target. Joint nonuniqueness is allowed; sampled alpha is projected to [0,1] and sampled 6-D rotation to SO(3).

contract.cut_relation: Covers every action in all twelve assigned [600,stop) segments without trimming. It preserves the complete 250-action [600,850) overlap per trajectory with red_transfer, totaling 3,000 supervised overlap actions through red release, transit, blue approach, closure and lift.
contract.output_semantics: Each unnormalized slot is [alpha, residual_x_m, residual_y_m, residual_z_m, world_rotation_6d(6), gripper]. At chunk sampling, b is the selected causal blue position and g is blue_goal. The world TCP position is b + clip(alpha,0,1)*(g-b) + residual. Label alpha is the clipped 3-D orthogonal projection of the demonstrated commanded TCP position onto the b-to-g segment; when squared endpoint separation is at most 1e-4 m^2, alpha is defined as 1. Rotation is world aligned and projected from 6-D to SO(3). Gripper retains demonstrated scalar/sign semantics. Slot 0 is t-1 and execution uses slots 1..8 for t..t+7. decode_action calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from freshly measured joints.
contract.parameter_semantics: source_object selects the causally observed blue_pose position b in world metres; destination_field selects the calibrated blue_goal position g in world metres. The selected endpoints are resolved and frozen at each chunk replan. They are semantic frame selectors, not arbitrary coordinates or actuator commands.
